value.rationale: This is a sharp all-length extinction classification for a canonical nontrivial finite-width lattice family. It identifies four discrete length thresholds with a final critical eleven-column trigger, quantitatively counts that natural minimal trigger event, and proves that the worst finite delay becomes typical in long random strips through independent local blocks. These properties are not routine renamings of the width-two result and supply concrete information about excitable propagation and finite-time nilpotency.
